Backend (src-tauri/src/lib.rs)

- probe_cli_binary now returns a parsed CliProbe (client, version, raw);
  select_default_binary ranks candidates bd>=floor > legacy bd > br >

- check_bd_compatibility payload is camelCase and adds binary, found,
  legacy, minSupportedMajor, searchedPaths (split with the platform
  PATH separator via std::env::split_paths)
- startup and get_bd_version/validate probes run from temp_dir and log
  searched directories when the binary is missing
- 29 Rust unit tests (18 new), including a serde camelCase contract test

Frontend
- app/utils/cli-compat.ts: pure status/dismissal helpers, 18 Vitest cases
- useCliCompatibility singleton: refresh on startup and after switching
  the binary in Settings; dismissal remembered per binary+version
- CliCompatibilityBanner under the header: non-dismissible error when
  the CLI is not found (with searched dirs + Settings link), dismissible
  warning for legacy bd / br; same status shown inside SettingsDialog
- useCliClient default is now 'bd' to match the backend fallback

0570a55a0238a9303af0e138b3ddbebe11f7723askillrxskillrx@hermesGitHubnoreply@github.com17892580292026-09-12T17:07:09-07:00cf94c5701351a7b9e832bace065e2e0e5355281bfix(cli): default to bd and detect it on GUI launchdefault_cli_binary() probed br before bd and, crucially, ran the
--version probe without the extended PATH that every other CLI call
uses. When the app is launched from Finder/Dock with a minimal PATH,
the probe cannot see Homebrew's bd, walks past it, and falls back to
br — which is not installed — producing 'br not found or not executable'
and breaking bd list for every project.

- Probe with get_extended_path() so the Homebrew binary resolves on
  GUI launches.
- Prefer bd (Go) over br (Rust) — the Dolt-era backend this app targets.
- Fallback default is now bd instead of br.
